🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A Dallas County jury found Dallas rapper Yella Beezy guilty of capital murder Wednesday, November 11, 2026, in the 2020 murder-for-hire killing of fellow rapper MO3 — exactly six years to the day after MO3 was shot and killed on Interstate 35 in Dallas.

Yella Beezy, 35, whose legal name is Markies Conway, was convicted of capital murder by remuneration, or murder for hire. Because prosecutors did not seek the death penalty, the conviction carries an automatic sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Prosecutors alleged Conway paid Kewon White $40,000 to carry out the killing. White, identified by prosecutors as the gunman, was convicted of capital murder in September 2026 and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Conway pleaded not guilty and denied any involvement in the killing, and he can appeal the verdict.

MO3, 28, whose real name was Melvin Noble, was driving on Interstate 35 in south Dallas around noon on November 11, 2020, when White pulled alongside him and opened fire, authorities said. Prosecutors said the killing grew out of a years-long feud between the two rappers.

A third defendant, Devin Brown, is also charged with capital murder in connection with MO3's death and is still awaiting trial.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram; CNN; XXL; AllHipHop.
